title: Census Trends: Sex Ratio, Literacy and Density

cards.b: Census data on population, sex ratio, literacy and density are used in prelims facts and mains arguments about demography and development. The last full census was in 2011. The next, delayed by the pandemic, has been announced for 2027 (with a caste count included). Know the 2011 figures cold and the trend over decades.

India's population in 2011 was 121.1 crore (1,210.8 million), about 17.5 percent of the world. Decadal growth was 17.7 percent in 2001-11, the lowest since Independence, down from 21.5 percent. Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state (19.98 crore); Sikkim the least. India overtook China as the most populous country in 2023, per UN estimates.

Stage 1: high birth and death rates. Stage 2: death rate falls, population rises. Stage 3: birth rate falls. Stage 4: both low. India is in the late stage 3: the total fertility rate (TFR) fell to about 2.0 (NFHS-5, 2019-21), below the replacement level of 2.1. The 1951-81 decades were the 'population explosion' period. The year 1921 is the Great Divide: after it population grew steadily.

Number of females per 1,000 males. India's 2011 ratio is 943, the highest since 1971. Kerala is highest (1,084), Daman and Diu (618) and Haryana (879 among states) are low. The child sex ratio (0-6 years) fell to 919 in 2011, the lowest ever, due to sex-selective abortion. The Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques Act (PCPNDT) 1994 targets this; Beti Bachao Beti Padhao started in 2015.

Literacy rate (age 7 and above) in 2011: 74.04 percent, with males 82.14 and females 65.46. Kerala highest (about 94 percent), Bihar lowest (about 62 percent). Lakshadweep and Mizoram do well among UTs and the Northeast. The gender gap has narrowed. Periodic Labour Force Survey data after 2011 give updates, and the 2023 'ULLAS' scheme runs adult literacy.

Population density in 2011 was 382 per sq km. Bihar is highest among states (1,106), then West Bengal (1,028). Arunachal Pradesh is lowest (17). Delhi has the highest overall (11,297). Density follows water and fertile land, so the Ganga plains are dense; the desert, the mountains and the Northeast are sparse.

Urban share rose to 31.1 percent in 2011. Census towns grew fast. The median age is about 28, so India enjoys a demographic dividend until about 2040-50. The working-age share is rising, but jobs, skills and women's participation (about 40 percent in recent surveys) decide whether the gain is realised. South India is ageing earlier.

The southern states reduced fertility earlier. If parliamentary seats are redistributed by population after 2026 (the freeze under Article 82 ends), they fear losing weight. The 15th Finance Commission also used the 2011 population, which raised similar concerns. Supporters of fresh delimitation say representation must follow people.

National Population Policy 2000, National Health Mission, and Mission Shakti. The Census is conducted under the Census Act 1948 and the Registrar General of India. Remember the first census (synchronous) in 1881, and the first after Independence in 1951.

Registrar General of India runs the Census and the Sample Registration System, which gives yearly birth and death data. NFHS gives fertility and health data, which fill the gaps between censuses.

Likely questions: 'Declining child sex ratio and remedies', 'Demographic dividend: opportunity or challenge?', 'Regional variation in literacy'.

  • Quote 2011 figures with the state extremes.
  • Always link numbers to cause and policy.
  • Note the next Census and the delimitation debate to show currency.

The Census asks about religion, language, scheduled castes and tribes, disability, migration and housing. The next Census will use digital data collection and, as announced, will count caste.
